newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Village Roadshow considers trust listing.
newsitem.headline: Village Roadshow considers trust listing.

text.p: Village Roadshow Ltd said on Monday that it had not made a final decision to proceed with the possible listing of a property trust.

The cinema operator and radio network group said in response to an article in The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper that it was in the early stages of considering an entertainment property trust as a a new business stream.
The newspaper said the company, which also operates theme parks, was looking at a A$200 million property trust listing.
The newspaper said the listing would allow the company to take its 10 stand-alone Australian cinema sites off the balance sheet and fund an aggressive expansion plan.
Brokerage firm SBC Warburg would manage and underwrite the float while Merrill Lynch would have an advisory role, it said.
"Village is in the early stages of considering and evaluating the establishment of an Entertainment Property Trust as a new business stream," the company told the Australian Stock Exchange.
"No final decision to proceed with the trust has been made," it said.

"The assets under consideration are owned in various joint ventures and partnerships and the book value of Village's equity in those assets is below any prescribed materiality or disclosure threshold," it said, referring to stock exchange announcement rules.
Village shares were three cents higher at A$4.95 at 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT).
